elements.element: Services performed in a professional manner
elements.evidence: "the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner"

elements.element: Services performed in a workmanlike manner
Software conforms to its applicable documentation
elements.evidence: "any software and Materials deliverable provided under this Agreement will conform to its applicable documentation"

elements.element: 30-day services warranty period measured from performance
elements.evidence: "The warranty in clause (i) applies for 30 days following performance of the applicable Services."
"Customer's remedy ... is repair, replacement, or a refund"
"repair, replacement, or a refund of the charges paid"
"or a refund of the charges paid for the non-conforming Services or software"
"for 90 days following delivery" — 90 days, not 12 months
"IBM covenants that it will comply with the laws applicable to IBM's business." (pre-existing, limited to IBM's business)
No malicious code warranty appears anywhere in the clause or insertion

reasons: The single insertion completes every atomic fallback element: professional and workmanlike Services standard, software conformance to documentation, 90-day software period, 30-day Services period measured from performance, and the repair/replacement/refund remedy set.
Preferred is not met (90 days rather than 12 months for software, 30 rather than 90 days for services, and no malicious-code warranty), which is expected given the locked fallback target.

Minimal: Section 5.1 contained no conformance warranty, period or remedy, so a concise added sentence block is the least intrusive fix; no other sentence was rewritten and no re-performance-only remedy was introduced.

Minor tension worth noting (not a deviation): the insertion covers "Materials" deliverables while paragraph (c) provides "ALL MATERIALS ... 'AS IS', WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND"; the express Section 5.1 warranty should control as the more specific and later-added term, but a carve-out in (c) would remove any argument.
Existing compliance-with-laws covenant is narrower than the playbook preference (limited to laws applicable to IBM's business); note in rationale only.
